features.headline: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
features.desc: The Pittsburgh passer is chasing records in his 22nd NFL season, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."
body: Entering his 22nd NFL season — or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" — the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.
In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots.
In Week 6 of 2026, he moved into a third-place tie with Peyton Manning with 539, and has since surpassed him this season with a total of 542 as of Week 10.

"Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

Rodgers supplanted Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in a loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025. But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that growing list of historic accomplishments.

Among the milestones for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 10 he has appeared in 296), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes.
And after Week 10, he needs 1,712 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards.
This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

features.headline: Which NBA players have the most triple-doubles of all time?
features.desc: Russell Westbrook holds the NBA record for most triple-doubles in a career. See who else joins him on the list.
body: Russell Westbrook has more than earned the nickname Mr. Triple Double.
In basketball, a triple-double is when a player compiles a double-digit total in three of five statistical categories (assists, blocks, points, rebounds and steals) over the course of a game.
Blocks and steals were officially recorded by the NBA starting in the 1973-74 season. No player in NBA history has recorded more triple-doubles than Westbrook.
On May 10, 2021, Westbrook became the NBA's career leader in triple-doubles, tallying 28 points, 13 rebounds and 21 assists for the Washington Wizards in a 125-124 loss against the Atlanta Hawks.
It marked the 182nd triple-double of Westbrook's career, passing Oscar Robertson for the most on the all-time list.
Nikola Jokić also has since passed Robertson, whose record stood for more than 47 years.
Westbrook had already broken Robertson's record for the most triple-doubles in a single NBA season (41), recording 42 during the 2016-17 campaign.

features.headline: Week 10 winners and losers: McCaffrey, Gibbs and Mahomes dominate Sunday
features.desc: Christian McCafffrey, Jahmyr Gibbs and Patrick Mahomes put fantasy teams on their back in Week 10, while Jonathan Taylor and the Packers and Panthers' passing games had quiet days.
features.by: Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft
body: Week 10 of the 2026 fantasy football season featured huge games by Christian McCaffrey, Jahmyr Gibbs, Patrick Mahomes and rookie Emmett Johnson. Meanwhile, Jonathan Taylor, Trey McBride, as well as the Green Bay and Carolina passing games, underperformed in a big way Sunday.
So, who were the big winners and losers around the league? Matt Bowen and Tristan H. Cockcroft offer their analysis.
Jump to a topic: Ranking winners | Ranking losers Biggest injuries and what's next
We have a new single-game high score for the season, as McCaffrey scored 46.3 fantasy points in a wild 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys.

He was dynamic as a runner, but his receiving prowess in this game was extraordinary, as he had a career-high 32.1 points on catches. That's remarkable considering he has 121 games played and 12 games of 10-plus catches.

By comparison, he had only four receptions in this game. The 49ers are doing a fine job keeping McCaffrey's 30-year-old legs fresh, though he does have two of his toughest matchups all season in the next two weeks (MIN, SEA).
He's a clear RB1, but don't expect nearly the same ceiling for those games. — Cockcroft
After a quiet Week 9, Gibbs roared back with a 44.2-point performance in Munich, reminding us why he's the No. 1 player in our game.
He tore up a New England Patriots defense that has been reeling the past two weeks; the Patriots surrendered a combined 80 points and 972 total yards to the Green Bay Packers and Lions.

Gibbs has exceeded 40 fantasy points in three of his past 16 regular-season games and 35-plus in seven of his past 20. His 253.4 points for the season is the eighth-most ever by a running back through his team's first nine games.

features.headline: Who has scored the most goals in NHL history?
features.desc: Alex Ovechkin holds the record for the most individual career goals in NHL history. Which other players are at the top of the list?
body: At the time of his retirement in 1999, Wayne Gretzky owned or shared 61 NHL records, including the mark for the most career goals. "The Great One" finished his illustrious 20-year career with an NHL-record 894 goals in 1,487 games. It is a mark that stood until Alex Ovechkin broke it in April 2025.

With Gretzky in attendance, Ovechkin scored his 895th career goal in a 4-1 loss to the New York Islanders. Ovechkin's record-breaking goal came in the 1,487th game of his NHL career, the same as Gretzky's career total.
The 2026-27 NHL season marks the 22nd for Ovechkin, who looks to add to his career goals total and put even more separation between him and the rest of the field.

features.headline: 2026-27 MLB free agency, trade grades: Offseason analysis
features.desc: We've got you covered with grades and analysis on every winter signing and big offseason trade.
body: The 2026-27 MLB offseason is officially here, and we have you covered with grades and analysis for every major signing and trade as this winter — which is expected to include a labor stoppage — unfolds.
Whether it's a franchise-changing free agent signing or an unexpected blockbuster trade, we'll weigh in with what it all means for next season and beyond.

ESPN MLB experts Bradford Doolittle and David Schoenfield will evaluate each move as it happens, so follow along here — this story will continue to be updated. Check back in for all the most recent analysis.

The Red Sox weren't high on anybody's list of teams likely to sign Jake Bauers given they already have an All-Star first baseman in Willson Contreras, but this signing is an early candidate for best move of the offseason.

The grade reflects two thoughts: (1) that Bauers' breakout — he finished 11th in the majors in OPS and third in on-base percentage this past season — is for real; and (2) that the contract is a steal at $14.5 million per year.

Bauers will be entering his age-31 season, and, of course, spent years struggling in the majors before finally figuring things out, so while there would generally be concern that his 2026 season was a fluke, all the advanced metrics suggest the opposite.
His Statcast numbers: 93rd percentile bat speed, 94th percentile hard-hit rate, 93rd percentile chase rate, 98th percentile walk rate.
Those are real skills that aren't going to diminish overnight and should allow him to remain a productive hitter (he even hit left-handers well, so should project as a full-time player).

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddya Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
First baseman Jake Bauers and the Boston Red Sox are in agreement on a four-year, $58 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Reliever Evan Phillips and the Atlanta Braves are in agreement on a three-year, $35 million contract.
Jacob Young agreed to terms on a long-term contract with the Washington Nationals, president of baseball operations Paul Toboni announced.

RHP Ryan Weiss agrees to $1.85M deal with San Diego Padres, sources say.

New York Yankees closer David Bednar, Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki and Seattle Mariners outfielder Randy Arozarena were among eight players who received $23.15 million qualifying offers from their teams Monday.
